title: M5Unit-8Encoder issue 7: uint8_t _speed truncation fixed in 7447df75, confirmed with a host harness

execution.environment: macOS; Apple clang 21.0.0; host C++ harness with mock Arduino/Wire headers; no Arduino core and no Unit-8Encoder hardware
commands: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -I include -I prefix prefix/UNIT_8ENCODER.cpp harness.cpp -o out/harness_prefix
g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -I include -I fixed fixed/UNIT_8ENCODER.cpp harness.cpp -o out/harness_fixed

checks.name: fix_present_in_source
checks.evidence: 7447df75:src/UNIT_8ENCODER.h:23 declares uint32_t _speed; begin() still takes uint32_t speed

checks.name: sda_scl_passthrough
checks.evidence: harness: Wire.begin() receives sda=21 scl=22 in both builds

checks.name: read_bytes_error_handling
checks.evidence: requestFrom() returning 0 still reads 4 bytes and returns -1; pre-existing gap outside this issue

checks.name: hardware_i2c_clock_measurement
checks.evidence: no Unit-8Encoder hardware and no ESP32-S3 board available

checks.name: arduino_core_wire_begin
checks.evidence: harness uses a mock TwoWire; the Arduino-ESP32 core divider/clamp path was not executed

checks.name: library_manager_release
checks.evidence: library.properties still says 0.0.1 and the only tag is 0.0.1; the fix is on main only

evidence.description: both harness runs plus sha256 of the headers and implementation used

notes: The merged fix changes only one line in src/UNIT_8ENCODER.h; src/UNIT_8ENCODER.cpp is identical before and after (sha256 034f6da8...).
The issue was authored by the reporter of the truncation and closed by M5Stack after PR #8 was merged.
